[1] Experts rubbish claims that clove and citrus are 'effective' dengue mosquito prevention

[2] - This article is more than three years old.

[3] - Published on June 20, 2023 at 07:59

[4] - 3 min read

[5] - By [AFP Sri Lanka](https://factcheck.afp.com/afp-sri-lanka)

[6] The Sinhala-language claim has been shared more than 26,000 times since it was posted on Facebook [here](https://archive.is/9rvkF) on May 27, 2023 alongside an image of citrus fruit with cloves stuck into the flesh.

[7] "Just do this minute task to keep dengue mosquitoes away. Take about four limes, cut them in half. Stick some new cloves in each half and place them near doors and windows," the post says.

[8] [Dengue](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/dengue-and-severe-dengue) -- a disease with symptoms ranging from fever, headache and joint pain to bleeding, organ failure and, in some cases, death -- is primarily spread by the Aedes aegypti mosquito that lays its eggs in standing water ([archived link](https://perma.cc/2ZLK-V2LP)).

[9] The Facebook post states mosquitoes that spread dengue cannot tolerate the combined smell of the fruit and spice and that the "repellent" should be replaced every two days.

[10] The claim this lime and clove combination acts as a natural repellent has circulated for years on social media, including on Facebook [here](https://archive.ph/NOexm), [here](https://archive.ph/OyatH) and [here](https://archive.ph/J4Nmz).

[11] It resurfaced with the false claim it could keep "dengue mosquitoes away" as Sri Lankan health authorities issued a [warning](https://www.presidentsoffice.gov.lk/index.php/2023/05/16/dengue-control-programs-implemented-continuously-throughout-the-country/) in May that cases of dengue in the country could surge and potentially surpass the previous year's record of 11,000 infections in June and July ([archived link](https://perma.cc/RXP8-5YAY)).

[12] This false claim was shared elsewhere on Facebook [here](https://archive.is/ftHbU) and [here](https://perma.cc/R6LE-H3PP), as well as on WhatsApp.

[13] But public health experts and an entomologist warned the public against considering it as a method to repel mosquitoes.

[15] [Dr Lahiru Kodituwakku](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Lahiru-Kodithuwakku) from the Sri Lankan Ministry of Health's National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) told AFP on June 15 the claim is extremely misleading and warned against relying on rumours circulating on socia

evidence.text:
[1] How to protect yourself from getting dengue fever

[2] Prevention is also based on protection against mosquito bites. Aedes mosquitoes show diurnal biting activities in both indoor and outdoor environments. Therefore, personal protective measures should be applied all day long and especially during the hours of highest mosquito activity (mid-morning and late afternoon).

[3] Personal protective measures to avoid mosquito bites should be applied when staying in dengue risk areas.

[4] - Using physical barriers such as Screening doors and windows of premises using mosquito proof meshes.

[5] - Protective clothes to cover the body specially for children those who do outdoor activities in the mornings and afternoons.

[6] - Application of natural repellents such as citronella oil, lemon grass oil, neem oil and chemical repellents containing DEET (N,N-Diethyl-m-toluamide). However, effects of repellents are short term. (½- 6 hours)

[7] - Repellent use must be strictly done in accordance with the instructions indicated on the product label.

[8] Dengue transmission is predominantly seen in urban areas, usually as family or immediate neighbourhood groups of patients (Clusters). Therefore, if a member of the family or anyone in the immediate neighbourhood is ill with dengue such patients and others should be protected from mosquito bites.

[9] Travellers, especially children, pregnant women, and people with immune disorders or severe chronic illnesses, should consult their doctor or seek advice from a travel clinic to receive personalized recommendations on use of repellents and protection before travelling

[10] Similar protective measures apply to symptomatic patients in order to prevent the disease from being transmitted to non-infected mosquitoes.

[6] Claim

evidence.text:
[1] The South African government has used NEC contracts to procure the first phase of its two newest universities. After a search for appropriate sites starting in 2011, Sol Plaatje University in Kimberley, Northern Cape Province and the University of Mpumalanga in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga Province were formally established in 2013.

[2] Both universities have been developed on existing sites, so much of the initial work involved the refurbishment of existing buildings. Sol Plaatje includes the former Kimberley Civic Centre and National Institute for Higher Education, while University of Mpumalanga occupies the site of Lowveld College of Agriculture, KaNyamazane Hospitality School and Siyabuswa Education Campus.

[3] The first 275 students enrolled in 2014 and were accommodated in the refurbished buildings while design of new buildings got underway. Construction started later that year, resulting in 16 new teaching, research, accommodation, welfare and administrative facilities being delivered by the start of the 2016 academic year – increasing the number of student places to nearly 2,000.

[4] Expert NEC team

[5] Given the complex scope and challenging timeframes, the government’s Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) appointed the experienced Campus Development and Planning unit at University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg to lead the project management team. ‘Wits’ has successfully delivered 35 of its own building projects worth R1.5 billion (£80 million) using NEC contracts.

[6] Wits capital projects manager Spencer Hodgson says, ‘We adopted NEC on our capital works programme in 2008 to promote a culture change from the traditional ‘them and us’ approach to one of collaboration. 结论：该声明有措辞依据，但省略了影响含义的语境，不能简单判为虚构或完全准确。

报道引语与较长录像的自动字幕均记载，Wilson 谈到网上“making fun of members of Congress”（嘲弄国会议员）的人，随后表示“they should be prosecuted”（他们应该被起诉）。[E11、E20、E24]

items.answer:
该声明基本属实：现有资料支持，弗吉尼亚州级官员曾多次要求返还这面战旗，并遭明尼苏达州长拒绝。[E6][E9]

涉事旗帜是弗吉尼亚第28志愿步兵团的邦联战旗，1863年7月3日在葛底斯堡战役中被明尼苏达第1志愿步兵团士兵缴获，后来纳入明尼苏达历史学会馆藏。[E2][E3]

具体而言，2000年弗吉尼亚州议员提出返还要求，明尼苏达州长Jesse Ventura拒绝；据2017年《先锋报》回顾，2003年包括弗吉尼亚州长Mark Warner在内的官员再次索旗，明尼苏达州长Tim Pawlenty也明确拒绝。[E6][E9]

范围限制：历史上的请求还包括民间组织请求，2013年的请求则是借用，不能全部算作州政府要求永久归还。[E6][E9] 尚未取得双方往来函件及2000年决议的最终表决记录，因此不能确认正式州际请求的总次数。

evidence.text:
[1] Virginia Mounts New Charge to Get Back Flag

[2] -   Share via

[3] During Pickett’s Charge, the futile and final Confederate assault of the Battle of Gettysburg, a bloodied and battered flag from a decimated Virginia infantry group was seized by a private from Minnesota, who claimed the souvenir as a spoil of war.

[4] One hundred thirty-seven years later, Virginians are mounting another charge, albeit a far more civil one, to get the flag back.

[5] Spurred by the fervor of a re-enactors group in Roanoke, a group of state senators from southwestern Virginia has put forth a resolution asking Minnesota to return the flag to its southern home.

[6] “It’s a matter of state pride,” said Sen. John S. Edwards (D-Roanoke), a sponsor of the resolution. “Minnesota has refused to return the flag, and they ought to. I don’t know why they need it.”

[7] Minnesota officials say they need the flag for the same reason Virginia wants it: as an important reminder of their state’s role in the Civil War.

3. 文件时长与声音：A长10.20秒，B长4.04秒，相差6.16秒；总时长差不能直接换算为播放倍速。（E3、E4）A文件有0条音轨，B有1条音轨。（E3、E4）B尚未试听或取得转写，因此声音内容及其对画面理解的影响未知；A文件无音轨也不能证明原始拍摄无声。

现有证据未建立全段连续对应，无法确定完整删减、重排或变速方式，也未确认B的来源身份及两份材料的制作先后关系。未检查的区间和声音内容不能视为没有差异。

[1] Just after a devastating [attack](https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-crash-hollande-idUSKCN0ZV08R?mod=related&channelName=worldNews) in Nice, France, on 14 July 2016 — in which dozens of people were killed and still more wounded when a man identified as French-Tunisian drove a huge truck through a large crowd watching fireworks — rumors spread thick and fast, as they do after any mass casualty event.

[2] Nine hundred kilometers away in Paris, Bastille Day celebrants saw smoke begin to billow up around the Eiffel Tower — the result of an accidental [explosion](https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/panic-huge-plumes-smoke-billow-8425417) of fireworks being trucked across the nearby Jena Bridge — and must have thought Paris itself was under attack. But it wasn't, and the structure itself was never in flames.

[3] Fear-mongering extremist and conspiracy web sites seized upon photos and [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cv_F3UkbdbI) of the event, however, misleadingly presenting them as "evidence" that the entire country was under coordinated attack. The Paris Police were quick to douse this speculation via social media. "Don't spread false rumors," read a boldface tweet from the Préfecture de police. "No fire at the #TourEiffel. An accidental truck fire took place at Jena Bridge. It has been put out."

items.task: 核查以下声明，必要时检查给定媒体并搜索外部证据。依据实际证据回答，说明结论范围与不确定性：The consumption of hot cross buns has the potential to affect breathalyzer readings.
items.answer:
结论：有条件成立。食用热十字面包后立即进行呼气酒精检测，可能因口腔残留酒精而出现短暂偏高的读数。Breathalyser公司网站报道其另行测试得到类似结果，并将原因解释为口腔酒精干扰。[E29]

给定视频约23秒时仪器显示“.000”，约50秒时显示“.018”。这些画面确认了显示值的变化，但单凭它们不能证明变化由面包造成，也不能将数值直接认定为真实血液酒精浓度。[E21、E17]

这种干扰具有明确的机制依据：美国FMCSA指南指出，口腔酒精可能造成人为偏高的读数，因此其确认检测程序要求初筛后等待至少15分钟，等待期间不得进食或饮水。这是特定检测制度的要求，不能视为所有地区的统一规定。[E33]

因此，该声明所说的“可能影响读数”有证据支持，但不能延伸为“吃面包会导致醉酒”。现有面包测试报道缺乏完整实验方法和配对血液检测，无法确定影响的发生概率、幅度，以及适用于所有产品和仪器的消退时间。[E29、E27]

evidence.provenance: 来源：外部网页 snopes.com
evidence.text:
[1] Blowing into a breathalyzer with food on your breath can result in inaccurate readings.

[2] The ingestion of a hot cross bun would not trigger a false positive if the breathalyzer were used properly.

[3] On 5 January 2018, the Facebook Page of the Australian trucking company “Pilbara Heavy Haulage Girls Inc.” posted a video alerting viewers that eating a hot cross bun (i.e., a spiced sweet bun made with currants or raisins) could affect the reading of a device commonly used by police to estimate blood alcohol content (BAC) from a breath sample:

[4] To make this point, the trucker in the video blew into a breathalyzer to produce a 0.000 reading, demonstrating that she had not consumed any alcohol. Then, after taking a bite of the pastry, she blew into the machine again directly after swallowing the food, charting a 0.018 BAC reading.

[5] Without undertaking any investigative efforts of their own, the UK tabloid The Sun made the unsupported [extrapolation](https://archive.fo/Yp610") that “just two buns would probably produce a result of more than the UK legal limit of 0.08.” Taking this idea one step further, the Daily Mail [claimed](https://archive.fo/F58w2") that “eating just one hot cross bun could get you ARRESTED this Easter.”

[6] These claims were hogwash in the context of any properly performed breathalyzer test. Professional breathalyzer devices such as the one shown in the above video rely on the assumption that the material being blown through them is 100% alveolar air -- that is, respired air directly from the lungs. A well-established [relationship](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400516300624) exists between the amount of alcohol in one's blood and the amount of alcohol in respired air from the lungs. The relationship is simple, 1:2100 blood alcohol to breath alcohol content, but that ratio only holds up in the absence of any other source of alcohol that could be introduced into the air blown through the breathalyzer. items.task: 比较给定视频 A 与候选视频 B，调查两者可由材料确认的差异及其对画面含义的影响。引用具体证据，说明差异所在位置和未能确定的内容。给定候选不代表已经确认其来源身份；不要把未检查的区域或模态视为没有差异。

proposed_tasks.task: 对照视频 A、B，核验左下角标题区除文字、字体外是否还有透明程度或渐变呈现的差异。具体疑点是：0秒对应帧 E5、E7 中，B 的蓝色标题底板似乎透出背景，而 A 的底板较为不透明；结合后续对应画面判断这一外观差异是否成立。说明可确认的位置、时刻或时间范围及其对背景可见性和标题呈现的影响，引用实际证据，保留无法区分的原因，不据此外推具体编辑方式或制作先后。
比较给定视频 A 与候选视频 B 在各自约4.84秒材料内的音频，核验是否存在可确认的声音或言语内容差异，以及这些差异是否影响对画面含义的理解。若有可辨认言语，核验其是否提供与画面标题“A conversation about CRPS”相关的内容依据。引用具体证据，说明差异时间位置；无法听清、无法比较或无法判断的内容保持未知，不根据标题推定实际谈话内容或人物诊断，不推定候选视频来源身份。
